subject: pathology
title: Sickle Cell Anaemia: HbS, Sickling, and Autosplenectomy

steps.tx: A single beta chain substitution, glutamate to valine at position six, lets deoxygenated haemoglobin polymerise into rigid sickles that obstruct microcirculation and haemolyse early. That one amino acid exchange creates **sickle cell anaemia (HbS)** disease when homozygous. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Glutamate to valine at beta six: one substitution, a lifetime of sickling, occlusion, and haemolysis.

vis.caption: Blood smear in sickle cell anaemia showing sickled red cells and target cells.

steps.tx: Polymerisation needs deoxygenation, acidosis, dehydration, cold, and infection as accomplices, while fetal haemoglobin and alpha thalassaemia trait dilute HbS and protect, explaining wide severity variation between patients. The polymerisation trigger state is **deoxygenated HbS polymerisation**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Oxygen protects and dehydration betrays: sickling follows deoxygenation, acidosis, cold, and infection.

steps.tx: The sickling test deoxygenates blood with metabisulfite to force sickling on a slide, screening cheaply but failing to separate trait from disease, which electrophoresis and HPLC accomplish by quantifying fractions. Screening and confirmation divide between **sickling test and HPLC quantification**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: The sickling test screens, HPLC decides; a positive sickle test cannot tell trait from disease.

left.title: Sickling (solubility) test
points: False negatives in severe anaemia, infancy

steps.tx: Repeated splenic infarction in childhood scars the spleen into a shrunken fibrotic remnant, removing its filtering function while the child still needs it against encapsulated bacteria. This self inflicted splenectomy is **autosplenectomy**, usually complete by five years of age. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: The spleen infarcts itself away by age five in sickle cell disease; vaccinate as for a splenectomised child.

vis.caption: Hyposplenism blood film with Howell-Jolly bodies, the marker of lost splenic function.

steps.tx: Howell-Jolly bodies, nuclear remnants a working spleen would have pitted out, appear on film as splenic function fails, alongside target cells and irreversibly sickled forms. Their presence is a free functional assay: **Howell-Jolly bodies of hyposplenism**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Howell-Jolly bodies on the film are the spleen's resignation letter; read them as lost splenic function.

rows: Seen in HbC, liver disease, thalassaemia

steps.tx: Newborn screening catches disease before the first sequestration or pneumococcal sepsis, letting penicillin prophylaxis, pneumococcal and meningococcal vaccination, and parent education prevent early deaths. Early diagnosis through **newborn haemoglobinopathy screening** transformed childhood survival. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Newborn screening plus penicillin and vaccines is why children with sickle disease now survive childhood.

right.title: With screening
points: Diagnosis in first weeks of life
Parents taught splenic palpation, fever action

steps.tx: Chronic haemolysis drives its own complications: pigment gallstones, leg ulcers, priapism, avascular necrosis of femoral heads, and proliferative retinopathy accumulate beside the acute crises. Annual surveillance hunts them early; the burden is **chronic sickle vasculopathy**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Between crises, haemolysis and vasculopathy quietly injure hips, eyes, kidneys, and lungs; surveillance hunts them yearly.

steps.tx: Hydroxycarbamide raises fetal haemoglobin, diluting HbS polymerisation and cutting crises, acute chest, and mortality, yet remains underused from exaggerated fertility and malignancy fears. Offering it to every eligible patient is **hydroxycarbamide (hydroxyurea) disease modification**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Hydroxycarbamide raises HbF and saves lives in sickle disease; offer it rather than reserving it for the worst cases.
